title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
gist: Janet Zhou argues civil-society oversight of public finances is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance but its grant funding is collapsing; she proposes earmarking about 5% of stolen-asset recoveries and sovereign-debt treatment savings for independent oversight funds.

insights.claim: In 2021 Zimbabwean Finance Minister Mthuli Ncube issued more than $15 million in guarantees for private loans to the Commercial Bank of Zimbabwe without seeking parliament's approval, an example of a common practice of committing state resources to non-essential projects.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Illustrates contingent-liability and hidden-debt risk in frontier sovereigns.

insights.claim: Zimbabwe's High Court ordered the government in March 2023 to gazette a bill on parliament's role in approving loans and guarantees, but the bill was drafted and never gazetted, and the deadline passed with no action.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
entities: Zimbabwe Coalition on Debt and Development
insights.so_what: Court wins without funded enforcement capacity do not change sovereign borrowing behavior.
insights.locator: Consider the order that we won

insights.claim: Aid from OECD donors fell by 23.1% in real terms in 2025, the largest annual drop ever recorded, collapsing the grant model for financing public accountability in developing countries.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Shrinking aid removes a key external check on borrower governments' debt disclosure.
insights.locator: This model of financing public accountability

insights.claim: Zimbabwe's April 2025 Private Voluntary Organisations Amendment Act allows authorities to cancel civil-society registration and seize assets without judicial oversight, and El Salvador's May 2025 Foreign Agents Law imposes a 30% tax on all foreign funding.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Governance risk is rising in both countries as civil-society constraints tighten.
insights.locator: Zimbabwe's Private Voluntary Organisations Amendment Act

insights.claim: Agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments could each include a clause directing a fixed share, with 5% a justifiable starting point, to independent oversight of public finance in the recipient country.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Watch for such clauses in future restructurings and asset-return deals.
insights.locator: The answer may lie in two types of international instruments

insights.claim: Precedents exist: Switzerland repatriated roughly $321 million stolen by Sani Abacha in December 2017 under an agreement with World Bank monitoring and civil-society oversight, and Ecuador's 2023 debt-for-nature swap pays roughly $12 million annually for 18.5 years into a governed Galapagos fund.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Creditors have already accepted ring-fencing terms, so oversight earmarks are feasible in restructurings.

insights.claim: The Sevilla Commitment calls for strengthening parliamentary debt oversight, independent audit institutions and civil society's role in exposing illicit financial flows, but nobody has said who pays for that work.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
entities: Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development
insights.so_what: Implementation gap in the financing-for-development agenda.
insights.quote: But nobody has said who pays for that work.

insights.claim: Because a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund its auditors, writing the obligation into settlements makes the money survive the next budget or election and gives creditors insight into the borrower's disclosure practices.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Creditors gain disclosure visibility, lowering hidden-debt risk in restructurings.
insights.quote: A borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it.
insights.locator: But when the obligation is written

insights.claim: Research tracking undisclosed-debt revelations across 154 countries over a century found nearly half of all sovereign defaults coincided with substantial upward revisions to reported public debt.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Funded outside scrutiny is a leading indicator for hidden-debt surprises preceding default.

insights.claim: Oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance because properly funded outside scrutiny begins long before a default and can pave the way for reform.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: Favors credit analysis that weights transparency and independent oversight capacity.
insights.quote: Oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance.

insights.claim: At the October IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings the new Borrowers' Platform, meant to give developing countries a stronger voice in global debt discussions, held its first Governing Council; the author says finance-minister coordination must be coupled with long-term external funding for civil-society watchdogs.
insights.speaker: JANET ZHOU
insights.so_what: New institution to watch in sovereign-debt architecture reform.
insights.locator: As efforts to revamp the global financial architecture accelerate
